children.text: Hello and welcome to Austin Community College Spotlight. My name is Ed Lundy. I'm Student Programs Officer for Austin Community College, and the Spotlight is about the people and programs of the college, trying to help the community understand us better.
My co-host today is, luckily, is Yvonne Estes, biology instructor at the college. Welcome, Yvonne.
Yvonne, today's program is about part-time faculty and, well, the That which makes the college grow and go in many ways. And you as a full-time instructor, you depend upon them.

We really do. We have a wonderful collection in the biology department. Many of them are doing research or have done research on the frontiers of science. And one of the things that they contribute to the students is the excitement of research and what it's like to be on the cutting edge. And I think that excitement is something that you can read about it in books, but when someone tells you what the problems are, because they've been there, or they're there right now, it's something that is very, very good for the students.

And the first person we're going to talk with today is Arnold Garcia, who's the news editor of the Metropolitan Section of the Austin American Statesman. Our first segment, Mr.Garcia. It's going to be fun.

The spotlight's here this afternoon at the news desk of Mr. Arnold Garcia, who's the Metropolitan Editor of the Austin American Statesman. We're here because Mr. Garcia is a faculty member at ACC, and we've come to his place of employment not only to learn something about him, but something about how a newspaper is put together. Mr. Garcia, hi.

I said to our audience that we were going to talk not only about the newspaper, but about faculty who teach here. But first of all, tell us something about yourself and how you got to the newspaper world.

Well, I started out working for my hometown newspaper, the San Angelo Standard Times, as a reporter in 1969 and then, or 1968 rather, and then I got drafted in '69 and went away to the Army and came back and I've been in the newspaper business ever since.

This is really exciting for me. This is the whole world of newspapers kind of revolving around here. Do you feel up the middle of things here at your big desk? This is the biggest desk I've ever sat at.

Well, actually there are two people who sit here. I have a fellow to work with. And what we do here is we lay out the city state section. We take the space that determined by the amount of advertising we sell and we put the news in it.
Well, as the metropolitan editor, you're responsible for what?
I am responsible for the makeup, the look, and the story selection of the B section, the city-state section.
It's 11:15 now, and your day is beginning. When does it reach its apex then?

It gets pretty exciting about 11:15 when we have a production deadline. We have to be off the floor, our pages, all our pages have to be in off the floor for the first edition and back to engraving in 11:15.
Are all these people who are out here who are clapping you on here and giving you praise, are they part of your area?

Well, they're part of my working family, yes sir. The news editor, my immediate supervisor, would sit in that chair there in the middle. Over there you see what we call the national desk. Actually it's international and national news and the fellow who sits in the middle is the national editor, he's away right now. And what they do is compile the national and international report.
